description: Playwright settings tab within the runner Settings panel. Configures authentication credentials and environment variables for Playwright test execution. Contains two card sections: 'Test Authentication' (username/email + password with show/hide toggle) and 'Environment' (base URL + skip web server toggle). Password is stored securely in the OS keychain and displayed as '********' on load. Settings are persisted via Tauri IPC commands (get_playwright_settings / save_playwright_settings). The four settings fields map directly to environment variables passed to Playwright tests: PLAYWRIGHT_TEST_USERNAME, PLAYWRIGHT_TEST_PASSWORD, PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL, and SKIP_WEB_SERVER.

groups.name: Page Structure
groups.description: The Playwright settings tab renders a SectionHeader with title 'Playwright Tests' and a description about authentication credentials and environment configuration, followed by two card sections ('Test Authentication' and 'Environment'), a Save Settings button row, and an informational 'How it works' box. There are no sub-tabs or nested navigation within this tab.

assertions.description: A heading with text 'Playwright Tests' is present as the section title
A description reading 'Configure authentication credentials and environment for Playwright test execution.' is visible below the heading

criteria.textContent: Configure authentication credentials and environment for Playwright test execution.

assertions.description: Two card sections are always visible: 'Test Authentication' and 'Environment'. Both are unconditionally rendered — there are no tabs, toggles, or loading gates that would hide either section.

groups.name: Test Authentication Section
groups.description: The 'Test Authentication' card contains a description explaining that credentials are passed as PLAYWRIGHT_TEST_USERNAME and PLAYWRIGHT_TEST_PASSWORD environment variables, a Username or Email text input, and a Password input with a show/hide toggle button.

assertions.description: A section heading with text 'Test Authentication' is present within the authentication card
A text input with id='test-username', labeled 'Username or Email', and placeholder 'user@example.com' is present
A password input with id='test-password', labeled 'Password', and placeholder 'Enter password' is present. By default it renders as type='password' (characters masked).

Clicking the Eye/EyeOff icon button adjacent to the password input toggles the input between type='password' (masked) and type='text' (visible). The button icon switches from Eye to EyeOff when the password is shown. Toggling visibility does not modify the stored value or trigger a save.
assertions.precondition: The password input is rendered and contains a value

assertions.description: The authentication card contains a description that mentions 'PLAYWRIGHT_TEST_USERNAME' and 'PLAYWRIGHT_TEST_PASSWORD' environment variables, explaining that credentials are passed to tests for authentication.

groups.name: Environment Section
groups.description: The 'Environment' card contains a Base URL optional text input (passed as PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL) and a 'Skip Web Server Startup' toggle switch (sets SKIP_WEB_SERVER=1 when enabled). The Base URL field has a helper text explaining the fallback to playwright.config.ts. The Skip Web Server toggle defaults to enabled (on).

assertions.description: A section heading with text 'Environment' is present within the environment card
A text input with id='base-url', labeled 'Base URL (optional)', and placeholder 'http://localhost:3001' is present
A helper text reading 'Passed as PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL. Leave empty to use the default from playwright.config.ts' is visible below the base URL input

A toggle row labeled 'Skip Web Server Startup' with description 'Assume the web server is already running. Sets SKIP_WEB_SERVER=1' is present. The toggle is a custom button that switches between the primary color (enabled) and muted color (disabled).

target.label: Skip Web Server Startup toggle row

assertions.description: The Skip Web Server Startup toggle defaults to enabled (on) when settings have never been saved. This reflects the Rust default of `skip_web_server: true` in the PlaywrightSettings struct. The toggle button should have the primary background color class applied when enabled.
assertions.precondition: Playwright settings have never been saved (fresh installation or cleared settings)

groups.name: Save Settings Action
groups.description: A 'Save Settings' button at the bottom of the form persists all four settings via the save_playwright_settings Tauri IPC command. The button is disabled when no changes have been made (hasChanges=false) or while saving is in progress (isSaving=true). After any field is modified, the button becomes enabled. On successful save, 'Playwright settings saved' is emitted as a success log, and the button returns to the disabled state.

assertions.description: A button with text 'Save Settings' is present at the bottom of the form
On initial load (before the user modifies any field), the Save Settings button is disabled. It has the muted/grey styling class and the `disabled` attribute. The user cannot click it.
assertions.precondition: Page has loaded and no field has been modified yet

assertions.description: After modifying any of the four settings fields (username, password, base URL, or skip web server toggle), the Save Settings button becomes enabled — it switches from grey/muted to the primary color and the `disabled` attribute is removed.
assertions.precondition: At least one field has been modified since the last save or page load

assertions.description: Clicking the enabled Save Settings button invokes the save_playwright_settings Tauri IPC command with the current field values. On success, a 'success' level log message 'Playwright settings saved' is emitted and the Save button returns to the disabled state. On failure, an 'error' level log message is emitted and the button remains enabled so the user can retry.
assertions.precondition: Save Settings button is enabled (at least one field has been changed)

assertions.description: While save is in progress (between click and IPC response), the Save Settings button displays 'Saving...' instead of 'Save Settings' and is disabled. The button returns to 'Save Settings' once the IPC call completes.
assertions.precondition: Save has been triggered and the IPC call is pending

groups.name: Password Security Model
groups.description: The password field has special security behavior: the actual password is stored in the OS keychain (Windows Credential Manager, macOS Keychain, Linux Secret Service), never in the plaintext settings.json file. When loading settings, the Rust backend returns '********' in the test_password field if a password is stored. Saving '********' unchanged does not overwrite the real password. Saving null/empty clears the password from the keychain.

assertions.description: When a password has been previously saved, the password input displays '********' on page load (not the real password). This indicates the keychain holds a password. If no password is set, the password input is empty on load.
assertions.precondition: Page has loaded after a previous save that included a password

assertions.description: If the user loads the page (seeing '********'), makes no change to the password field, and saves other fields, the real password in the OS keychain must not be overwritten. The Rust backend skips keychain writes when the submitted value is '********'. The original password remains valid for subsequent Playwright test runs.
assertions.precondition: Password field shows '********' from a previous save and the user saves without modifying the password

assertions.description: The password is stored exclusively in the OS keychain under key 'PLAYWRIGHT_PASSWORD'. The settings.json config file never contains the plaintext password (the test_password field in the persisted JSON is always null). A new real password typed by the user (not '********') replaces the keychain entry on save. An empty/null submission deletes the keychain entry.

groups.name: How It Works Info Box
groups.description: An informational box at the bottom of the form (below the Save button) explains how the settings are used at test runtime. It references the process.env variable names and mentions the auth.setup.ts file that reads these variables to log in and save the browser session.

assertions.description: A bold 'How it works:' label is present at the start of the info box
The info box contains two inline code elements showing 'process.env.PLAYWRIGHT_TEST_USERNAME' and 'process.env.PLAYWRIGHT_TEST_PASSWORD', demonstrating how tests access the credentials at runtime.

groups.name: Settings Load on Mount
groups.description: When the Playwright settings tab is first rendered, it automatically calls get_playwright_settings via Tauri IPC to populate the form with previously saved values. This runs asynchronously on mount. If the call fails, an error is logged but the form remains functional with default values.

assertions.description: On opening the Playwright settings tab, the form is populated with the previously saved values: username in the username input, '********' in the password input (if a password exists), base URL in the base URL input, and the skip web server toggle reflecting the saved boolean. The Save button remains disabled until the user modifies a field.
assertions.precondition: Settings have been previously saved at least once

assertions.description: If the get_playwright_settings IPC call fails (e.g., Tauri backend error), an error-level log message starting with 'Failed to load Playwright settings:' is emitted. The form retains its default initial values (empty username, empty password, empty base URL, skip_web_server=true). The user can still edit and save settings.

groups.name: Environment Variable Mapping
groups.description: Each of the four settings fields maps to an environment variable that is injected when Playwright tests run. The spec defines this mapping so workflows can verify the correct env vars are documented and the correct fields are present. The UI descriptions on the page itself expose this mapping to the user.

assertions.description: The page documents that four settings map to environment variables: test_username → PLAYWRIGHT_TEST_USERNAME, test_password → PLAYWRIGHT_TEST_PASSWORD, base_url → PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL (optional, falls back to playwright.config.ts default when empty), skip_web_server → SKIP_WEB_SERVER=1 (set only when the toggle is on). These mappings are visible in the UI descriptions and helper texts on the page.
The Skip Web Server Startup toggle description reads 'Assume the web server is already running. Sets SKIP_WEB_SERVER=1', making clear the exact env var name and value set by this toggle.

states.name: Settings Loaded — No Changes
states.description: The Playwright settings form has loaded its values from the backend. No field has been modified. The Save Settings button is disabled (grey, cursor-not-allowed).

transitions.name: Modify a field
transitions.description: Type in the username, password, or base URL input, or click the Skip Web Server toggle to enable changes

states.name: Settings Modified — Unsaved Changes
states.description: At least one field has been modified since the last save or page load. The Save Settings button is enabled (primary color, clickable).

transitions.name: Click Save Settings
transitions.description: Click the enabled Save Settings button to trigger the save IPC call

states.name: Saving in Progress
states.description: The save IPC call is in progress. The button shows 'Saving...' text and is disabled. Transitions automatically to pw-unmodified on success, or back to pw-modified on error.

transitions.name: Save completes successfully
transitions.description: After the IPC call returns success, the button reverts to 'Save Settings' (disabled) and hasChanges resets to false
